answer: The premise is mistaken. Node2vec does not extend the collective classification procedure, and it does not use graph kernels. Node2vec (Grover & Leskovec, 2016) is a representation-learning method. It generates node sequences with second-order biased random walks, controlled by a return parameter p and an in-out parameter q, and then feeds those sequences into a skip-gram model (word2vec-style) to learn low-dimensional node embeddings. Those embeddings are typically used as features for a standard classifier, such as logistic regression, in a supervised node classification setup. Collective classification, such as iterative classification or label propagation, is a separate family of methods that iteratively infers labels by exploiting correlations among neighboring nodes' labels. Node2vec does not modify that inference loop. Graph kernels are a different tool, used for comparing graphs or nodes via kernel functions. Node2vec is not a graph kernel method, although it is sometimes compared with kernel-based approaches.
